card: Introduces a BlockRequestTracker to automatically retry failed manual block downloads across alternative peers. Currently, getblockfrompeer requires choosing an explicit peer and silently abandons the download if that peer disconnects or fails to respond. The change makes peer selection optional in getblockfrompeer, retries failed downloads by default, and tracks pending manual requests within the P2P block scheduler. This is part of the tracking project for prune node rescan (#29183) and addresses issue #27652.
evidence: PR description: "This was requested by users because the getblockfrompeer RPC command lacks the functionality to notify them about block request failures or peer disconnections (which is expected due to the asynchronous nature of the block requests)."
Connected to user issue #27652 ('Allow getblockfrompeer to use any peer') and tracking issue #29183 ('Prune Node Rescan Project Tracking').
problem: The getblockfrompeer RPC requires users to specify an explicit peer ID and initiates a fire-and-forget request. If the specified peer disconnects or stalls, the caller is not notified and the node does not automatically attempt to fetch the block from another peer.
scope_notes: Adds a standalone BlockRequestTracker class with its own mutex, hooks into PeerManagerImpl::FindNextBlocksToDownload and FinalizeNode to manage pending on-demand downloads, and modifies the getblockfrompeer RPC interface.
summary: Introduces a BlockRequestTracker to manage and retry on-demand block downloads across peers in the P2P layer. Updates the getblockfrompeer RPC to make peer_id optional and add a retry boolean parameter defaulting to true. When enabled, failed or timed-out requests to a peer are returned to a pending queue and dispatched to another capable peer during regular block download scheduling.
